rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing humanity, Ibn Kathir says knowledge of the first creation proves resurrection a fortiori; nothing should lead a person who knows this to deny recompense.
rows.anchor: بالجزاء في المعاد وقد علمت البدأة ،   وعرفت أن من قدر على البدأة ،   فهو قادر على الرجعة بطريق الأولى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid rejects the idea that the address concerns the Prophet; it concerns the human being, as Ikrima and others also say.
rows.anchor: قلت لمجاهد : { فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِالدِّينِ } عنى به النبي

rows.speaker: عكرمة وغيره
rows.claim: Ikrima and others likewise identify the human being, rather than the Prophet, as the one addressed.
rows.anchor: عنى به الإنسان .   وهكذا قال عكرمة وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the most just judge and wrongs no one; His justice includes raising the dead to let the oppressed receive justice against their worldly oppressors.
rows.anchor: الذي لا يجور ولا يظلم أحدًا ،   ومن عَدْله أن يقيم القيامة فينصف المظلوم في الدنيا ممن ظلمه .

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits a Prophetic instruction to answer the surah's final verse, after reciting it, by affirming that God is the wisest judge and that one bears witness to this.
rows.anchor: وقد قدمنا في حديث أبي هريرة مرفوعًا :  " فإذا قرأ أحدكم { وَالتِّينِ وَالزَّيْتُونِ } فأتى على آخرها : { أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَحْكَمِ الْحَاكِمِينَ } فليقل : بلى

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha recounts the beginning of revelation: the Prophet first saw true dreams, then loved retreat and worship at Hira, where Gabriel commanded him to read and pressed him three times before revealing the opening verses.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة قالت : أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

rows.speaker: خديجة
rows.claim: Khadija reassures the shaken Prophet that God will never disgrace him, citing his kinship care, truthful speech, support of the burdened, hospitality, and aid in hardship.
rows.anchor: فقالت له : كلا أبشر فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبدا ؛ إنك لتصل الرحم ،   وتصدُق الحديث

rows.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
rows.claim: Waraqa identifies the visitor as the messenger who came to Moses, predicts the Prophet will be driven out, and wishes he could live to support him.
rows.anchor: فقال ورقة : هذا الناموس الذي أنزل على موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says this report is transmitted in both Sahih collections and notes that he discussed its chain, text, and meanings at length in his Bukhari commentary.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحديث مخرج في الصحيحين من حديث الزهري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These opening verses were the first Qur'an revealed, the first mercy and blessing to humanity; they recall creation from a clot and God's honoring of people by teaching what they did not know, the distinction by which Adam excelled the angels.
rows.anchor: وهُنَّ أول رحمة رَحم الله بها العباد ،   وأول نعمة أنعم الله بها عليهم .   وفيها التنبيه على ابتداء خلق الإنسان من علقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge takes mental, spoken, and written forms; written knowledge entails the other two, while mental or spoken knowledge need not be written.
rows.anchor: والعلم تارة يكون في الأذهان ،   وتارة يكون في اللسان ،   وتارة يكون في الكتابة بالبنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An aphorism urges preserving knowledge by writing it down.
rows.anchor: وفي الأثر : قيدوا العلم بالكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another aphorism says that whoever acts on what he knows will be granted knowledge of what he did not know.
rows.anchor: " من عمل بما علم رزقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir classifies Surat al-Humaza as Meccan.
rows.anchor: تفسير سورة ويل لكل همزة لمزة وهي مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamz is criticism by speech and lamz by action: the offender belittles and disparages people; Ibn Kathir links this to the description in 68:11.
rows.anchor: الهماز : بالقول ،   واللماز : بالفعل .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the pair as one who continually abuses and finds fault.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ } طعان معياب .

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas distinguishes hamz as attacking someone to his face and lamz as doing it behind his back.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس : الهمزة ،   يهمزه في وجه ،   واللمزة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the offender attacks with tongue and eye, backbites people, and criticizes them.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : يهمزه ويلمزه بلسانه وعينه ،   ويأكل لحوم الناس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says hamz is done with hand and eye, while lamz is done with the tongue.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : الهمزة : باليد والعين ،   واللمزةُ : باللسان

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd gives the same distinction as Mujahid: hand and eye for hamz, tongue for lamz.
rows.anchor: واللمزةُ : باللسان .   وهكذا قال ابن زيد

rows.speaker: مالك عن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Malik transmits from Zayd ibn Aslam that a hamzah is someone who consumes people's flesh through backbiting.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك ،   عن زيد بن أسلم : هُمَزة لحوم الناس .

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify the person targeted by the warning as al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq.
rows.anchor: ثم قال بعضهم : المراد بذلك الأخنس بن شريق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported view says the warning concerns someone other than al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq.
rows.anchor: بن شريق ،   وقيل : غيره .

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the warning is general rather than limited to a particular person.
rows.anchor: وقيل : غيره .   وقال مجاهد : هي عامة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rejects the offender's assumptions; the person who amassed and counted wealth will certainly be cast into al-Hutamah, a name for the Fire because it crushes whoever enters it.
rows.anchor: أي : ليس الأمر كما زعم ،   ولا كما حسب .   ثم قال تعالى : { لَيُنْبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ } أي : ليلقين هذا الذي جمع مالا فعدده

rows.speaker: ثابت البناني
rows.claim: Thabit al-Bunani says the Fire burns its inmates up to their hearts while they remain alive; he says the torment has reached them and weeps.
rows.anchor: قال ثابت البناني : تحرقهم إلى الأفئدة وهم أحياء ،   ثم يقول : لقد بلغ منهم العذاب

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says the Fire consumes the whole body, reaches the heart near the throat, then returns over the body.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب : تأكل كل شيء من جسده ،   حتى إذا بلغت فؤاده حَذْوَ حلقه ترجع على جسده .

rows.speaker: ثابت البناني
rows.claim: Thabit al-Bunani says the Fire burns its inmates up to their hearts while they remain alive; he says the torment has reached them and weeps.
rows.anchor: قال ثابت البناني : تحرقهم إلى الأفئدة وهم أحياء ،   ثم يقول : لقد بلغ منهم العذاب

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says the Fire consumes the whole body, reaches the heart near the throat, then returns over the body.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب : تأكل كل شيء من جسده ،   حتى إذا بلغت فؤاده حَذْوَ حلقه ترجع على جسده .

rows.speaker: ثابت البناني
rows.claim: Thabit al-Bunani says the Fire burns its inmates up to their hearts while they remain alive; he says the torment has reached them and weeps.
rows.anchor: قال ثابت البناني : تحرقهم إلى الأفئدة وهم أحياء ،   ثم يقول : لقد بلغ منهم العذاب

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says the Fire consumes the whole body, reaches the heart near the throat, then returns over the body.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب : تأكل كل شيء من جسده ،   حتى إذا بلغت فؤاده حَذْوَ حلقه ترجع على جسده .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire is shut over them; Ibn Kathir points back to his explanation in Surat al-Balad.
rows.anchor: أي : مطبقة ،   كما تقدم تفسيره في سورة البلد .

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits a Prophetic gloss of mu'sadah as shut or closed.
rows.anchor: عن أبي صالح ،   عن أبي هريرة ،   عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : { إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ } قال :  " مطبقة

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: A parallel transmission gives the same gloss as Abu Salih's own statement, without raising it to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن أبي صالح قوله ،   ولم يرفعه .

rows.speaker: عطية العوفي
rows.claim: Atiyya al-Awfi says the extended pillars are made of iron.
rows.anchor: قال عطية العوفي : عمد من حديد .

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the extended pillars are made of fire.
rows.anchor: وقال السُّدِّي : من نار .

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ikrima transmits Ibn Abbas's interpretation that the extended structures are the doors.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة ،   عن ابن عباس : { فِي عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ } يعني : الأبواب هي الممدوة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: In the reading of Abdullah ibn Masud, Qatada reports wording that explicitly says the Fire is closed with extended pillars.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : إنها عليهم مؤصدة بعمد ممدة .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Awfi transmits from Ibn Abbas that inmates are put in extended pillars, supports are stretched over them, and chains around their necks seal the doors.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي ،   عن ابن عباس : أدخلهم في عمد فمدت عليهم بعماد ،   وفي أعناقهم السلاسل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they used to report that the inmates are tormented with pillars in the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : كنا نحدث أنهم يعذبون بعمد في النار .

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers the report that the inmates are tormented with pillars in the Fire.
rows.anchor: في النار .   واختاره ابن جرير .

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih interprets the extended pillars as long fetters.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح : { فِي عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ } يعني القيود الطوال .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The canonical codex separates this surah from al-Fil with a basmala, although Ibn Kathir says it is connected in meaning to the preceding surah.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مفصولة عن التي قبلها في المصحف الإمام ،   كتبوا بينهما سطر بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ،   وإن كانت متعلقة بما قبلها .

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam connect the surahs: God held the elephant army back from Mecca and destroyed its people, setting up the favor to Quraysh.
rows.anchor: كما صرح بذلك محمد بن إسحاق وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم ؛  لأن المعنى عندهما : حبسنا عن مكة الفيل ،   وأهلكنا أهله .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of Quraysh's ilaf is their harmonious life together in a secure homeland.
rows.anchor: أي : لائتلافهم واجتماعهم في بلدهم آمنين .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is their customary winter trade journey to Yemen and summer journey to Syria, with safe return because people respected them as residents of God's sanctuary; even travelers joining them were safe.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بذلك ما كانوا يألفونه من الرحلة في الشتاء إلى اليمن ،   وفي الصيف إلى الشام في المتاجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their safety while settled in Mecca is also illustrated by God's making the sanctuary secure while people around it were seized; this verse explains the first phrase by apposition.
rows.anchor: كما قال الله : { أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا حَرَمًا آمِنًا وَيُتَخَطَّفُ النَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ } [ العنكبوت : 67 ] ولهذا قال : { لإيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ } بدل من الأول ومفسر له .

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers taking the lām as an exclamatory lām: marvel at Quraysh's settled life and God's favor to them; he cites Muslim agreement that the surahs are separate and independent.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جرير : الصواب أن  " اللام "  لام التعجب ،   كأنه يقول : اعجبوا لإيلاف قريش ونعمتي عليهم في ذلك .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In gratitude for this great favor, Quraysh should worship God alone, Lord of the House, who made their sanctuary safe and their House sacred; Ibn Kathir links the command to 27:91.
rows.anchor: ثم أرشدهم إلى شكر هذه النعمة العظيمة فقال : { فَلْيَعْبُدُوا رَبَّ هَذَا الْبَيْتِ } أي : فليوحدوه بالعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir classifies the two refuge surahs as Medinan.
rows.anchor: تفسير سورتي المعوذتين وهما مدنيتان .

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b says Gabriel instructed the Prophet to recite both surahs, which the community follows despite Ibn Masud's omission.
rows.anchor: قلت لأبي بن كعب : إن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud erased the surahs and reportedly said the Prophet ordered seeking refuge by them, not reciting them; another report says he called them outside God's Book.
rows.anchor: عن علقمة قال : كان عبد الله يَحُك المعوذتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says Ibn Masud may not have heard them or received them by tawatur, and may have later returned to consensus, since the Companions included them in official codices sent everywhere.
rows.anchor: ولم يتواتر عنده ،   ثم لعله قد رجع عن قوله ذلك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Uqba reports the Prophet saying that no verses like these two were revealed on that night.
rows.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: On a journey, the Prophet taught Uqba the two as among the best surahs, recited them in prayer, and told him to read them at bedtime and on waking.
rows.anchor: فتقدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأ بهما ،   ثم مر بي

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet ordered Uqba to recite the two refuge surahs after each prayer; al-Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb.
rows.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر قال : أمرني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Uqba to recite the two surahs, saying that he would read nothing comparable.
rows.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر قال : قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: While riding with Uqba, the Prophet repeatedly had him recite al-Falaq and warned him not to slight it; nothing he prayed with was comparable.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says people have not sought refuge with anything like the two surahs.
rows.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر ؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet teaches Uqba both surahs and says no petitioner or seeker of refuge has asked or sought with anything like them.
rows.anchor: ثم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عند ذلك :  " ما سأل سائل

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Uqba reports that the Prophet recited the two surahs in the dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ بهما

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: Uqba says he asked for Hud or Yusuf, and the Prophet replied that nothing was more beneficial with God than al-Falaq.
rows.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر قال : اتبعت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet names the two refuge surahs to Ibn A'ish al-Juhani as the best protections people seek.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له :  " يا ابن عائش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir judges Uqba's many routes close to mass transmission, giving certainty to many hadith specialists.
rows.anchor: فهذه طرق عن عقبة كالمتواترة عنه ،   تفيد القطع

rows.speaker: صدي بن عجلان وفروة بن مجاهد
rows.claim: A report says no counterpart to al-Ikhlas and the two refuge surahs was revealed in the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Furqan.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في رواية صُدَيّ بن عجلان ،   وفَرْوَةَ بن مُجَاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In another travel report, the Prophet recites both surahs with a man and tells him to read them in prayer; Ibn Kathir thinks the man is Uqba.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن هذا الرجل هو عقبة بن عامر ،   والله أعلم .

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prompts Abdullah al-Aslami ibn Unays to recite al-Ikhlas and both refuge surahs, then teaches him this way of seeking protection.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وضع يده على صدره ثم قال

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Jabir to recite the two refuge surahs and says he will read nothing like them.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال : قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says the Prophet recited the two surahs, blew into his palms, and wiped them over his head, face, and front of his body.
rows.anchor: وتقدم حديث عائشة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ بهن

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: When sick, the Prophet recited them over himself and blew; when his illness worsened, Aisha recited and rubbed his hand for blessing.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا اشتكى

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Abu Said reports that the Prophet sought protection from jinn and human eyes, then used the two surahs and left other protections; al-Tirmidhi calls the report hasan.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يتعوذ

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir and many early authorities gloss al-Falaq as dawn; al-Qurazi, Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Jarir link it to 6:96.
rows.anchor: عن جابر قال : الفلق : الصبح .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses al-Falaq as creation; al-Dahhak agrees and says the Prophet should seek refuge from all creation.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة ،   عن ابن عباس : { الْفَلَقِ } الخلق .

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says al-Falaq is a chamber in Hell whose opening makes its people cry from intense heat.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار : { الْفَلَقِ } بيت في جهنم

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي عن آبائه
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ali and his forefathers call al-Falaq a covered pit at Hell's bottom, emitting fire so hot that Hell cries out; Amr ibn Abasa and al-Suddi share this view.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن علي ،   عن آبائه أنهم قالوا : { الْفَلَقِ } جب في قعر جهنم

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي عن أبي هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra through Muhammad ibn Kab calls al-Falaq a covered pit in Hell; Ibn Kathir cites Ibn Jarir's judgment that it is not sound as a Prophetic report.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي ،   عن أبي هُرَيرة ،   عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن الحبلي
rows.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli says al-Falaq is one of Hell's names.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الرحمن الحبلي : { الْفَلَقِ } من أسماء جهنم .

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers al-Falaq as dawn; Ibn Kathir calls it correct and notes al-Bukhari chose it too.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جرير : والصواب القول الأول ،   أنه فلق الصبح .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer seeks protection from the evil of every created thing.
rows.anchor: أي : من شر جميع المخلوقات .

rows.speaker: ثابت البناني والحسن البصري
rows.claim: Thabit al-Bunani and al-Hasan al-Basri specify Hell, Iblis, and his descendants among the created things whose evil is feared.
rows.anchor: وقال ثابت البناني ،   والحسن البصري : جهنم وإبليس وذريته مما خلق .

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the darkening as night entering at sunset; Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn Kab, al-Dahhak, Khusayf, al-Hasan, and Qatada describe night arriving with darkness.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : غاسقُ الليلُ إذا وقبَ : غُروبُ الشمس ،   حكاه البخاري عنه .

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri interprets the darkening as the sun when it sets.
rows.anchor: وقال الزهري : { وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ } : الشمس إذا غربت .

rows.speaker: عطية وقتادة
rows.claim: Atiyya and Qatada say that when night has entered, waqaba means that it has gone away.
rows.anchor: وعن عطية وقتادة : إذا وقب الليل : إذا ذهب .

rows.speaker: أبو المهزم عن أبي هريرة
rows.claim: Abu al-Muhazzim transmits from Abu Hurayra that al-ghasiq is a star.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو المهزم ،   عن أبي هريرة : { وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ } كوكب .

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says Arabs called the fall of the Pleiades al-ghasiq, associating its setting with more illness and plague and its rising with their decline.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : كانت العرب تقول : الغاسق سقوط الثريا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet from Abu Hurayra says al-ghasiq is the dark star; Ibn Kathir says this report is not sound as a Prophetic attribution.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هُرَيرة ،   عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  { وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ } قال : النجم الغاسق

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir also reports a view identifying al-ghasiq as the moon.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جرير : وقال آخرون : هو القمر .

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet pointed to the rising moon and told her to seek God's protection from its evil as the darkening body when it sets; al-Tirmidhi grades this hadith hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة ،   رضي الله عنها : أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيدي ،   فأراني القمر حين يطلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretations converge: the moon is a sign of night and stars shine only at night, so their harm falls under the evil of night as it enters.
rows.anchor: قال أصحاب القول الأول وهو أنه الليل إذا ولج : هذا لا ينافي قولنا ؛ لأن القمر آيةُ الليل ،   ولا يوجد له سلطان إلا فيه

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة والحسن وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: Mujahid, Ikrima, al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak interpret those blowing on knots as sorceresses; Mujahid explains that they chant spells and blow into the knots.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد ،   وعكرمة ،   والحسن ،   وقتادة والضحاك : يعني : السواحر .

rows.speaker: طاووس
rows.claim: Tawus warns that few things come closer to associating partners with God than incantations for snakebite victims and the mentally ill.
rows.anchor: عن ابن طاوس ،   عن أبيه قال : ما من شيء أقرب من

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: In another report, Gabriel recites a healing prayer over the Prophet against every harmful illness, envy, and the evil eye, asking God to heal him.
rows.anchor: فقال : بسم الله أرقيك ،   من كل داء يؤذيك ،   ومن شر كل حاسد وعين ،   الله يشفيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir suggests this may have been during the Prophet's illness when he was bewitched; God healed him, frustrated the Jewish sorcerers' scheme, exposed them, and spared the Prophet from confronting them.
rows.anchor: ولعل هذا كان من شكواه ،   عليه السلام ،   حين سحر ،   ثم عافاه الله تعالى وشفاه ،   ورد كيد السحرة الحسَّاد من اليهود

rows.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Arqam reports that a Jewish man bewitched the Prophet with knots in a well; Gabriel disclosed the plot, Ali retrieved them, and after they were undone the Prophet recovered as if released from a tether and never confronted the Jew.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن أرقم قال : سحر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلٌ من اليهود ،   فاشتكى لذلك أياما

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that Labid ibn al-Asam bewitched the Prophet with a comb and its fibers hidden in a male palm spathe beneath a stone in Dhruwan well; he imagined relations with his wives that had not happened, and two angels disclosed the cause and means.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه ،   عن عائشة قالت : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سُحر ،   حتى كان يُرَى أنه يأتي النساء ولا يأتيهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Aisha's report, the Prophet retrieves the object, declines to publicize or retaliate against the culprit because he does not want to stir evil among people, and the well is ordered buried.
rows.anchor: فقال :  " أمَّا اللهُ فقد شفاني ،   وأكره أن أثير على أحد من الناس شرًا "

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعائشة
rows.claim: Al-Thaalabi gives a more elaborate version: a Jewish servant passed the Prophet's hair and comb fragments to Labid, who hid them in the well; after six months of illness, Ali, al-Zubayr, and Ammar retrieved a twelve-knot cord, and each revealed verse undid a knot until the Prophet recovered.
rows.anchor: وقال الأستاذ المفسر الثعلبي في تفسيره : قال ابن عباس وعائشة ،   رضي الله عنهما : كان غلام من اليهود يخدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says al-Thaalabi gives this version without an isnad; it is strange and partly very objectionable, although some details have corroborating reports.
rows.anchor: هكذا أورده بلا إسناد ،   وفيه غرابة ،   وفي بعضه نكارة شديدة ،   ولبعضه شواهد مما تقدم

none: Verse text only; the segment contains no commentary.
